chapter: Taped excerpts: friends, family and facts
title: Thurgood Marshall as a neighbor
summary: Johnson lived in the same Manhattan building as Thurgood Marshall and knew his first wife.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And now we have some more excerpts of various tapes, which we will scatter through here.
(Inaudible).
Yeah. Things are fine, thank you. I'm delighted to hear you don't have the hiccups.
No. No.
That's good. You up to a few questions?
Yes.

Wonderful. All right. One of the things that I was thinking is that you know a good cross section of people, not only in the music line. And one of the people you once mentioned to me is Thurgood Marshall. That goes back a long time. Could you tell me how you met?
Well, we used to live in the same building. It was the normal thing to know people in the same building. (Inaudible).
Right. Where was that, J. C.?
140 (Branast) Avenue.
Uh-huh. Is that when you were living in St. Albans?
No, (Branast) Avenue is in Manhattan.
Oh, it is?
Just the other side of Rich Avenue.
Oh, see that. All right. Now, did you ever have any indication then that he would go as far as he has today?
Oh, of course not.
Did he marry you?
Marry who?
Did he marry you and Julie?
Oh, no.
No? Uh-huh. What's his wife like?
Well, I don't know his present wife. I knew the other wife.
No, I meant the wife that you knew.
Oh, she was very lovely, very nice person.
- - - (Microphone interference)
(Inaudible).
Would you like us to send him a copy of the latest J. C. Johnson Newsletter?
Oh, I don't know if that would mean much to him. He's up so high now, he can't look down.
You want to know something? I don't think he'd be looking down at all. I think he'd be looking across.
Well --
